Title: Discovery and citation harvest
Description: Search arXiv for the landmark papers behind each of the four scaling levers; fetch BibTeX by arXiv ID, never by hand
Acceptance: ref.bib holds 8 entries with no PLACEHOLDER_ prefix; every entry reproducible from an arXiv ID
Notes: Fetched with arxiv_registry.py fetch-bibtex. DBLP title search was tried first and returned a wrong match for "Adam", which is why lookup is by ID here.

Title: Evidence pack assembly
Description: Map each of the four levers to the citations that support it, before any prose is written
Acceptance: Each outline section has at least one citation assigned
Notes: Trivial at this size; the mapping lives in the plan outline rather than in a separate evidence-packs/ directory.

Title: Introduction
Description: Frame the scaling question and name the four levers the review covers
Acceptance: Reader knows the scope and what is out of scope by the end of paragraph two
Notes: Stage 1 outline then Stage 2 prose, per references/writing-style.md.

Title: Architecture and optimization
Description: Residual connections and adaptive optimization as the two things that made depth trainable
Acceptance: Explains the trade-off each made, not just the headline result
Notes: Figure fig:timeline is a TikZ timeline; no external image file, so nothing to break on a clean checkout.

Title: Pre-training and transfer
Description: The shift from task-specific training to pre-train-then-adapt
Acceptance: Table contrasts the four levers on what they changed and what they cost
Notes: Table is hand-built with booktabs and p{} columns rather than resizebox, per the layout hygiene rules in SKILL.md.

Title: Efficient adaptation and limitations
Description: Why full fine-tuning stopped being affordable; then state honestly what eight citations cannot support
Acceptance: Limitations section names the coverage gap explicitly
Notes: The Limitations section is not decoration: format_gate.py checks for it at venues that mandate it.

Title: Anti-AI writing scan
Description: Scan every section for AI-typical phrasing and rewrite what it flags

Title: Citation verification
Description: Confirm every citation key in main.tex resolves to a verified ref.bib entry and that no claim overstates its source
Acceptance: verify_citations.py reports no unresolved or unverified keys

Title: Privacy and anonymity scan
Description: Confirm no secrets, absolute local paths, or author identity leaked into the sources
Notes: arXiv is not double-blind, so anonymity_check is run here as a demonstration rather than as a requirement.

Title: Compile and page count
Description: Compile to PDF with no undefined citations and no overfull hbox
Acceptance: compile_paper.py exits 0; no "Citation undefined" in the log

Title: Format gate against a real venue
Description: Run format_gate.py with --venue neurips to show what the gate reports for a paper not written for NeurIPS
Acceptance: Gate output is understood and its FAILs are expected and explained in the plan
Notes: Expected result: FAIL on the missing Broader Impact section and the missing style file. That is the correct answer, not a bug.

Title: arXiv packaging
Description: Build the submission tarball and read the generated report
Acceptance: submission.tar.gz builds with no blocking problems; .bbl is embedded
Notes: Run: python scripts/arxiv_package.py --project-dir examples/minimal-review-paper --dry-run. The tarball itself is not committed.
